strengths: Novel application of learning-to-learn to zeroth-order LLM optimization with practical 'train once, reuse widely' motivation
Well-grounded theoretical analysis via Theorem 1 showing per-block variance adaptation improves convergence bounds under block-diagonal Hessian assumptions
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across 28 task-model combinations with thorough ablations, learning rate sensitivity analysis, and memory/time overhead quantification
Elegant technical design with minimal overhead: <3.4% computational cost, <2MB additional memory for OPT-30B, via compact per-block neural networks
Strong reproducibility support with detailed implementation details, clear hyperparameter specifications, and algorithm descriptions
Consistent empirical improvements: 82.1% task-model combinations outperform MeZO baseline with 2.5% average accuracy gain
weaknesses: Critical gap: cross-architecture generalization completely untested—only tested transfer within same model family (LLaMA variants). No evidence optimizer trained on LLaMA transfers to Qwen or OPT, contradicting the 'train once, reuse widely' vision central to the motivation
Block-diagonal Hessian assumption only approximately holds; no empirical validation of actual block-diagonality in tested models or sensitivity analysis when assumption is violated
Unjustified approximation during L2L training: gradient flow is blocked through finite-difference estimator to save memory, lacking theoretical analysis of impact on convergence

Questionable COPA dataset selection for L2L training based on 'smooth loss decrease' and 'fast cycles'—appears somewhat arbitrary; limited multi-dataset comparison (C.5 shows single-dataset sometimes outperforms, unexplained)

Improvement magnitudes modest with high variance: wide error bands in Figure 2 (especially WSC), several task-model pairs show minimal gains within noise; 82.1% is convergence speed metric, not final accuracy
Substantial L2L meta-training overhead despite 'one-time cost' framing: 2.4× normal fine-tuning time, ~51 min GPU time for OPT-30B; unclear if investment scales across realistic task distributions
Incomplete PertNN architecture analysis: fixed design (2-layer MLP, 64 units) across all blocks without ablations on depth, capacity, or sensitivity to design choices
Unfixed L2L hyperparameters (η₁=10⁻⁶, η₂=10⁻², ε=10⁻³, reset period) appear selected without justification or sensitivity analysis

Loose connection between theory and practice: Theorem 1 provides bounds under ideal assumptions, but method learns variances from compressed statistics (mean/variance); tightness of this connection unclear
Limited evaluation horizon: experiments use 10k-20k steps; generalization to longer training trajectories and potential optimizer drift unexplored

strengths: Well-motivated practical approach: The observation that a small set of base LLMs are repeatedly fine-tuned across tasks is compelling, and the 'train once, reuse widely' paradigm is practically valuable
Theoretically grounded with block-diagonal Hessian justification: Theorem 3.1 provides principled motivation for block-wise variance learning based on Transformer curvature structure
Clever scalable design with minimal overhead: Per-parameter-block lightweight MLPs achieve negligible memory (<2MB for OPT-30B) and time overhead (<3.4%) while enabling learned optimization

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Systematic evaluation on 4 LLMs and 7 datasets with strong baselines, extensive ablations, learning rate sensitivity analysis, and generalization tests across derivative checkpoints and longer-sequence tasks
Strong generalization: Single optimizer trained on COPA transfers reliably to other datasets and model variants, outperforming baselines in 82.1% of combinations
Excellent reproducibility: Extensive implementation details, hyperparameter grids, multiple ablations, and promised code release facilitate reproducibility
Robust to hyperparameter choices: Learning rate sensitivity analysis demonstrates the method is more robust than baselines across a wide range of learning rates
weaknesses: Informal theoretical justification: Theorem 3.1 provides upper bound improvement but relies on approximate block-diagonal Hessian assumption; no convergence guarantees provided, and gap between idealized theory and practice is unexplored

Missing cost-benefit analysis: Meta-training requires significant resources (332GB memory, 51 minutes for OPT-30B). Paper does not analyze breakeven point—how many downstream tasks justify this one-time cost? Critical for practitioners

Generalization mechanisms poorly understood: While empirical generalization is shown, why task-agnostic statistics (Mean, Var) transfer across fundamentally different tasks is unclear. Surprisingly, multi-dataset L2L training provides no substantial advantage (Section C.5), suggesting the optimizer doesn't learn deep task structure

Significant approximations under-analyzed: Gradient flow is cut off through the finite-difference term during L2L training to save memory (Appendix B.3). This substantial approximation affects optimizer learning but is dismissed with only 'strong empirical performance' mentioned; no ablation provided

Limited comparison with practical alternatives: Only compares against other zeroth-order methods; missing comparison with L2L baselines and no principled analysis of when ZO Fine-tuner is preferable to LoRA+quantization, which can also achieve low memory

Block-wise granularity not fully justified: Why Transformer parameter-blocks are the right unit is assumed rather than validated. No exploration of finer-grained (per-head) or coarser alternatives; effectiveness may be architecture-specific

Periodic reset mechanism appears ad-hoc: Resetting model parameters to address chronological bias in training data lacks principled justification. No ablations on reset frequency or exploration of alternative solutions (e.g., importance weighting)
Modest improvements in absolute terms: 2.5% average accuracy improvement and ~2.5% loss improvement are useful but incremental; gap to first-order methods remains (93% FO vs 92% ZO on some tasks)
Limited failure case analysis: Minimal improvements on WSC and other tasks; no analysis of failure modes or when task-specific optimization might be necessary

Incomplete L2L hyperparameter transparency: Section C.8 mentions tuning ε, η₁, η₂, reset schedule 'based on first-order trajectory behavior' but sensitivity to these choices and per-model tuning requirements are unclear
